targets.authors: Graham DS, Graham RR, Manku H, Wong AK, Whittaker JC, Gaffney PM
targets.title: Polymorphism at the TNF superfamily gene TNFSF4 confers susceptibility to systemic lupus erythematosus
targets.evidence_quote: A recent study demonstrated the association of TNFSF4 haplotypes located in the upstream region with risk for- or protection from Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) (Graham et al, 2008). In order to replicate this association, five single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) tagging the previously associated haplotypes and passing the proper quality control filters were tested in 1312 cases and 1801 controls from Germany, Italy, Spain, and Argentina.
targets.outcome_quote: The association of TNFSF4 with SLE was replicated in all the sets except Spain. There was a unique risk haplotype tagged by the minor alleles of the SNPs rs1234317 (pooled OR=1.39, p=0.0009) and rs12039904 (pooled OR=1.38, p=0.0012). We did not observe association to a single protective marker (rs844644) or haplotype as the first study reported; instead, we observed different protective haplotypes, all carrying the major alleles of both SNPs rs1234317 and rs12039904.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The paper explicitly confirms the risk association but contrasts its protective-haplotype result with the original, and reports no replication in Spain. General confirmation of genetic susceptibility is a specific positive comparison rather than an overall verdict resolving the expressly discordant protective finding.

reasoning: Independent case-control samples retest Graham et al. TNFSF4 associations. Other susceptibility-gene studies and original sample-source papers are background. The assigned online publication year 2008 and issue year 2009 identify the same article.
